symbols.name: p
symbols.def: \(p\) is the fixed number of observed variables.

symbols.name: CoefficientPair
symbols.def: \(B=(B_1,B_2)\), where \(B_{e,uv}\) is the coefficient on \(u\to v\).

symbols.name: InnovationPair
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\) is the pair of innovation vectors.

symbols.name: InnovationVariance
symbols.def: \(\omega=(\omega_v)_{v\in\mathbb V}\) is the innovation-variance vector shared by both environments.

symbols.name: BaselineCoefficientMatrix
symbols.def: \(B^*\) is the baseline coefficient matrix compatible with \(G^*\).

symbols.name: InterventionTargetPair
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I=(\mathcal I_1,\mathcal I_2)\), where \(\mathcal I_e\) lists targeted vertices.

symbols.name: CommonOrder
symbols.def: \(\pi\) is a topological order of \(G^*\) and hence of \(G_1,G_2\).

symbols.name: SCMPair
symbols.type: paired linear Gaussian structural causal model
symbols.def: \(M=(G^*,B^*,\mathcal I,G,B,\omega,\pi)\) is a baseline-indexed pair of environment SCMs.

symbols.name: DifferenceDAG
symbols.def: \(D(M)=(\mathbb V,E_D(M))\), where \(u\to v\in E_D(M)\) if and only if \(u\in\operatorname{Pa}_{G^*}(v)\) and \(B_{1,uv}\neq B_{2,uv}\).
symbols.role: Bystrova--Devijver difference DAG whose skeleton and orientations are learned by population LDiffPC.

symbols.name: DiffRelevantPath
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{DR}_M(\rho)\) holds for a path \(\rho\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\) exactly under \(\text{def:diff-relevant-path}\).
symbols.role: Definition 2 path predicate for changes that propagate without conditioning.

symbols.name: ConditionallyDiffRelevantPath
symbols.role: Definition 3 path predicate for changes induced through residualization.

symbols.name: DiffSeparation
symbols.def: \(A\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}B\mid S\) means that \(S\) diff-separates \(A\) from \(B\) under \(\text{def:diff-separation}\).
symbols.role: Definition 4 graphical relation linked to cross-environment regression equality.

symbols.name: DistributionPair
symbols.def: \(P_M=(P_{M,1},P_{M,2})\) is the observational law pair induced by \(M\).

symbols.name: CovarianceCoordinate
symbols.role: Parameter observed by the Gaussian experiment.

symbols.name: RegressionCoefficient
symbols.role: Ledger statistic and direct-effect functional on a valid door.

symbols.name: EqualitySepsetLedger
symbols.def: \(\mathcal L(s)\) is the exact complete ledger constructed in \(\text{def:exact-ledger}\).

symbols.name: LDiffPCOutput
symbols.role: Discovered partial difference graph at a candidate covariance.

symbols.name: CompletionFiber
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak F(s)\) is the exact compatible fiber in \(\text{def:completion-fiber}\).
symbols.role: All causal explanations retained at one covariance pair.

symbols.name: CovarianceConfidenceRegion
symbols.role: Joint exact confidence region for the covariance pair.

symbols.name: ConfidenceUnion
symbols.role: Boundary-honest confidence union for the causal triple.

symbols.name: BranchIndexSet
symbols.def: \(\mathbb B_p\) indexes realizable ledger, order, and target branches.

symbols.name: BranchCell
symbols.def: \(\mathcal S_b\subset\Omega_p\) is the covariance cell for branch \(b\in\mathbb B_p\).
symbols.role: A fixed ledger and compatible-completion regime.

symbols.name: BranchEffectMap
symbols.def: \(\theta_b(s)\) is the direct-effect triple obtained from the Cholesky predecessor regression for branch \(b\).
symbols.role: Smooth target map within one branch.

symbols.name: BoundaryPoint
symbols.def: \(s_0\in\Omega_p\) is a fixed positive-definite covariance boundary point.

symbols.name: AccessibleBranchSet
symbols.role: Branches locally reachable from the boundary point.

symbols.name: BoundaryLimitSet
symbols.def: \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\theta_b(s_0):b\in\mathbb B(s_0)\}\), using the continuous branch extensions.
symbols.role: Zeroth-order causal ambiguity at a ledger boundary.

symbols.name: GaussianCovarianceLimit
symbols.role: Covariance of the paired sample-covariance limit.

symbols.name: GaussianLimit
symbols.role: Limit noise in the local covariance experiment.

symbols.name: GaussianAcceptanceBody
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A_{\gamma}(h+\mathbb Z_0)\) is the product, over \(e=1,2\), of covariance-score ellipsoids centered at the corresponding block of \(h+\mathbb Z_0\), each with \(\chi^2_{p(p+1)/2,\sqrt{1-\gamma}}\) radius.
symbols.role: Local limit of the exact Wishart region.

symbols.name: ZerothOrderRandomSet
symbols.role: Boundary limit of the unscaled confidence union.

symbols.name: FirstOrderRandomSet
symbols.role: First-order confidence-union limit when all accessible targets agree.

symbols.name: RegularProductScoreImage
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P_{\gamma}(y;b_0,s_0)\) is the cone-aware product-score image constructed in \(\text{def:regular-product-score-image}\).
symbols.role: Regular-stratum first-order image after intersecting the Gaussian acceptance body with the accessible branch cone.

symbols.name: LocalModelSequence
symbols.def: \((M_N)_{N\ge1}\subset\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) satisfies \(s(M_N)=s_0+h/\sqrt N+o(N^{-1/2})\) within one branch \(b_0\in\mathbb B(s_0)\).

symbols.name: GenericConfidenceProcedure
symbols.def: \((D_N)_{N\ge1}\) is any confidence-set procedure based only on \(\mathcal Z_n\).
symbols.role: Competitor in the honesty lower bound.

symbols.name: ChainForkParameter
symbols.def: \((a,b)\) indexes the unbounded rescaled chain--fork observational-equivalence family.

symbols.name: ChainForkCovariance
symbols.role: Common law for the rescaled chain and fork.

symbols.name: ColliderVertex
symbols.def: For the three-variable audit only, \(p=3\) and \(W\) is the unique vertex in \(\mathbb V\setminus\{X,Y\}\).
symbols.role: Ambiguous predecessor in the positive witness.

symbols.name: ColliderCovariancePair
symbols.def: For \(p=3\), in coordinate order \(X,W,Y\), \(\boldsymbol\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}=(\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_1,\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_2)\), with \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&3/10&23/50\\3/10&1&8/25\\23/50&8/25&1\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_2=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&3/10&2/25\\3/10&1&57/100\\2/25&57/100&543/500\end{psmallmatrix}\).
symbols.role: Legal equality-boundary witness with a singleton direct-effect fiber.

symbols.name: ThreeVariableIdentifiedEffectSet
symbols.def: \(\Psi_3(s)\) denotes \(\Psi(s)\) on the model class \(\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{df}}\).
symbols.role: Dimension-scoped effect fiber used only by the three-variable collider audit.

symbols.name: BoundaryCommonTarget
symbols.def: At a boundary point satisfying \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\), \(\tau_0\) denotes the common accessible-branch target.
symbols.role: Center for the first-order Gaussian decision problem.

symbols.name: TangentRadius
symbols.role: Radius making the local parameter set bounded.

symbols.name: LocalParameterSet
symbols.role: Branch-labelled bounded parameter space for the Gaussian tangent experiment.

symbols.name: TangentObservation
symbols.def: Under local direction \(h\), \(\mathbb Y_h=h+\mathbb Z_0\sim\mathcal N(h,V_0)\).
symbols.role: Observation in the Gaussian tangent experiment.

symbols.name: AuxiliaryRandomizer
symbols.def: \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) is independent of \(\mathbb Y_h\) for every \(h\).
symbols.role: Permitted external randomization for local confidence rules.

symbols.name: RandomizedConfidenceRule
symbols.def: \(\delta(\mathbb Y_h,U)\) is a closed subset of \(\mathbb R^3\), and \(\delta\) is measurable for the Effros \(\sigma\)-field on \(\mathcal F(\mathbb R^3)\).
symbols.role: Decision rule class for the local diameter problem.

symbols.name: ExtendedDiameter
symbols.def: Set \(\operatorname{diam}(C)=0\) when \(C=\varnothing\) or \(C\) is a singleton, and otherwise set \(\operatorname{diam}(C)=\sup_{x,y\in C}\|x-y\|_2\), allowing the value \(+\infty\).
symbols.role: Loss applied to randomized closed confidence sets.

symbols.name: CoverageAdmissibleRuleSet
symbols.role: Rules with uniform branchwise coverage on the bounded tangent experiment.

symbols.name: LocalMinimaxValue
symbols.role: Infimal uniformly covered expected diameter in the bounded tangent experiment.

symbols.name: PublishedAnchorModelClass
symbols.type: class of paired linear acyclic SCMs
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{BD}}\) is the full, not necessarily Gaussian, Bystrova--Devijver anchor class in \(\text{def:bystrova-devijver-anchor-class}\).
symbols.role: Published anchor class for the broadened honesty converse.

symbols.name: CoefficientBound
symbols.def: \(B\ge1\) is the fixed uniform absolute bound on environment-specific structural coefficients.

symbols.name: BoundedCovarianceScale
symbols.role: Upper covariance spectral envelope in the bounded subclass.

symbols.name: BoundedCovarianceFloor
symbols.role: Lower covariance spectral envelope in the bounded subclass.

symbols.name: BoundedModelClass
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_{p,B}^{\mathrm{df}}\) is the coefficient/covariance-bounded subclass in \(\text{def:bounded-boundary-model-class}\).
symbols.role: Finite-diameter SCM subclass for the constant-factor minimax comparison.

symbols.name: BoundedIdentifiedEffectSet
symbols.def: \(\Psi_B(s)\) is the compatible-completion direct-effect fiber restricted to \(\mathcal M_{p,B}^{\mathrm{df}}\).

symbols.name: BoundedConfidenceUnion
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}^{B}_{n,\gamma}\) is the exact paired-Wishart projection through \(\Psi_B\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(e\in\mathbb E\) and \(v\notin\mathcal I_e\), the structural mechanism of \(v\) under \(B_e\) equals its mechanism under \(B^*\).
The two environments use the same innovation-variance vector \(\omega\).

For every ordered pair \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\), \(r_1(A,B\mid S)=r_2(A,B\mid S)\) if and only if \(A\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}B\mid S\), where diff-separation is evaluated on \(G_1\cup G_2\) relative to \(D(M)\).

standard.name: Bystrova--Devijver diff-faithfulness, arXiv:2606.13947v1, the named assumption following Definitions 2--4

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \(M\), the joint sample law is \(P_{M,1}^{n_1}\otimes P_{M,2}^{n_2}\).
For every \(b\in\mathbb B(s_0)\), the local rescalings \(t^{-1}(\overline{\mathcal S_b}-s_0)\) converge locally in the Painleve--Kuratowski topology to \(T_b(s_0)\) as \(t\downarrow0\).

standard.name: Chernoff regularity of local constraint sets

definitions.name: Baseline-oriented difference DAG
definitions.construction: For \(M=(G^*,B^*,\mathcal I,G,B,\omega,\pi)\), set \(D(M)=(\mathbb V,E_D(M))\) with \(E_D(M)=\{u\to v:u\in\operatorname{Pa}_{G^*}(v),\ B_{1,uv}\neq B_{2,uv}\}\). The directions are inherited from the baseline DAG.

definitions.name: Diff-relevant path
definitions.construction: A path \(\rho\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\) is diff-relevant when either it contains an edge of \(D(M)\), or it contains a non-endpoint vertex having an ancestor with at least one incoming edge in \(D(M)\).

definitions.name: Conditionally diff-relevant path
definitions.construction: Given \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\), a path \(\rho\) between \(A\) and \(B\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\) is conditionally diff-relevant relative to \(S\) when it is not diff-relevant and at least one condition holds: \(\rho\) contains a collider having a descendant in \(S\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\); \(\rho\) contains a non-collider connected by a path active given \(S\) to a vertex of \(S\setminus\rho\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\); or an endpoint of \(\rho\) has an incoming edge along \(\rho\) and a descendant in \(S\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\).

definitions.name: Diff-separation
definitions.construction: For distinct \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\), define \(A\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}B\mid S\) to hold exactly when \(S\) blocks every diff-relevant path and every conditionally diff-relevant path relative to \(S\) between \(A\) and \(B\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\).

definitions.name: Diff-faithful invariant-noise baseline-intervention class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}=\{M=(G^*,B^*,\mathcal I,G,B,\omega,\pi):\text{ass:linear-structural-equations, ass:baseline-parent-containment, ass:modular-interventions, ass:independent-gaussian-innovations, ass:invariant-innovation-variances, ass:positive-innovation-variances, and ass:diff-faithfulness hold}\}\).

definitions.name: Complete equality and sepset ledger
definitions.construction: For \(s=\operatorname{vech}(\boldsymbol\Sigma)\), record for every ordered \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and every \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\) whether \(r_1(A,B\mid S)-r_2(A,B\mid S)=0\), together with every separating set used by the population LDiffPC skeleton and collider rules; the resulting finite record is \(\mathcal L(s)\).

definitions.name: Population LDiffPC output
definitions.construction: Run the population version of BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC Algorithm 1 on \(\mathcal L(s)\): remove an adjacency when the ledger records an equality, store its sepsets, orient unshielded colliders, and exhaust Meek rules; denote the result by \(H(s)\).

definitions.name: Exact LDiffPC-compatible causal fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F(s)=\{M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}:s(M)=s,\ D(M)\text{ has exactly the skeleton of }H(s)\text{ and agrees with every orientation recorded by }H(s)\}\).

definitions.name: Compatible-completion direct-effect fiber
definitions.construction: \(\Psi(s)=\overline{\{(\alpha_1(M),\alpha_2(M),\alpha_1(M)-\alpha_2(M)):M\in\mathfrak F(s)\}}\subseteq\mathbb R^3\).

definitions.name: Exact covariance likelihood pivot
definitions.construction:
For \(S\succ0\), set \(T_{e,n}(S)=
u_e\{\operatorname{tr}(S^{-1}\widehat\Sigma_e)-\log\det(S^{-1}\widehat\Sigma_e)-p\}\), and obtain \(q_{p,
u_e}(a)\) from \(W\sim\operatorname{Wishart}_p(I_p,
u_e)\).

definitions.name: Exact paired covariance confidence region
definitions.construction: Let \(a_{\gamma}=\sqrt{1-\gamma}\) and set \(\mathcal R_{n,\gamma}=\prod_{e=1}^2\{S_e\succ0:T_{e,n}(S_e)\le q_{p,\nu_e}(a_{\gamma})\}\).

definitions.name: Test-inverted direct-effect confidence union
definitions.construction: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}=\overline{\bigcup_{s:\operatorname{vech}^{-1}(s)\in\mathcal R_{n,\gamma}}\Psi(s)}\).

definitions.name: Ledger and completion branch stratification
definitions.construction: Enumerate the finite baseline DAG, target-set, common-order, difference-DAG, exact-ledger-sign, LDiffPC-compatible orientation, and Cholesky cases; after clearing positive principal-minor denominators, project their polynomial equality and strict-inequality systems to covariance coordinates. Index the nonempty projected cells by \(b\in\mathbb B_p\), call them \(\mathcal S_b\), and attach the rational predecessor-regression target map \(\theta_b\).

definitions.name: Zeroth- and first-order boundary limits
definitions.construction: At \(s_0\), form \(\mathbb B(s_0)\), \(T_b(s_0)\), and \(\mathcal A_{\gamma}(h+\mathbb Z_0)\); retain \(\theta_b(s_0)\) at order zero exactly when \(T_b(s_0)\) meets the acceptance body, and at order one map every point in that intersection through \(D\theta_b(s_0)\), producing \(\mathcal K_h^{(0)}\) and \(\mathcal K_h^{(1)}\).

definitions.name: Cone-aware regular-stratum product-score image
definitions.construction: Let \(m=p(p+1)/2\). At a point \(s_0\) in the relative interior of the unique branch \(b_0\), write \(y=(y_1,y_2)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^m\), \(\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)=\mathcal A_{1,\gamma}(y_1)\times\mathcal A_{2,\gamma}(y_2)\), and \(J=D\theta_{b_0}(s_0)=(J_1,J_2)\) according to the two covariance blocks. Define \(\mathcal P_{\gamma}(y;b_0,s_0)=J\bigl(T_{b_0}(s_0)\cap\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)\bigr)\). If \(s_0\) is in the ambient interior of \(\mathcal S_{b_0}\), then \(T_{b_0}(s_0)=\mathbb R^d\), so \(\mathcal P_{\gamma}(y;b_0,s_0)=J\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)=J_1\mathcal A_{1,\gamma}(y_1)\oplus J_2\mathcal A_{2,\gamma}(y_2)\); if additionally \(\mathcal A_{e,\gamma}(y_e)=y_e+E_{e,\gamma}\) for its centered covariance-score ellipsoid \(E_{e,\gamma}\), then this set equals \(Jy+J_1E_{1,\gamma}\oplus J_2E_{2,\gamma}\).

definitions.name: Same-law chain--fork family
definitions.construction:
For every integer \(p\ge3\) and every \((a,b)\in\mathbb R^2\) with \(a\neq0\) and \(b\neq0\), choose \(W\in\mathbb V\setminus\{X,Y\}\) and enumerate the remaining vertices as \(\mathbb V\setminus\{X,Y,W\}=\{U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3}\}\).  When \(p=3\), this list is empty and every appended equation and order relation below is vacuous.  Use coordinate order \((X,Y,W,U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3})\).  In each environment of \(M^{\mathrm{ch}}\), define
\[
 X=\varepsilon_X,\qquad Y=aX+\varepsilon_Y,\qquad W=bY+\varepsilon_W,
 \qquad U_j=\varepsilon_{U_j}\quad(1\le j\le p-3),
\]
where all innovations are mutually independent centered Gaussians with variance one.  In each environment of \(M^{\mathrm{fk}}\), define
\[
 Y=\eta_Y,\qquad X=\frac{a}{a^2+1}Y+\eta_X,\qquad W=bY+\eta_W,
 \qquad U_j=\eta_{U_j}\quad(1\le j\le p-3),
\]
where all innovations are mutually independent centered Gaussians, with variance vector
\[
 \bigl((a^2+1)^{-1},a^2+1,1,\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{p-3}\bigr)
\]
in coordinate order \((X,Y,W,U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3})\).  Thus every \(U_j\) is independent of \((X,Y,W)\), has no incident edge, and has the same standard-Gaussian mechanism in both environments.  Within each paired SCM take the two environment coefficient matrices and innovation-variance vectors to be identical, take the displayed DAG and coefficient matrix as \((G^*,B^*)\), and take \(\mathcal I_1=\mathcal I_2=\varnothing\).  Use common orders obtained by appending \(U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3}\) to \(X\prec Y\prec W\) for \(M^{\mathrm{ch}}\) and to \(Y\prec X\prec W\) for \(M^{\mathrm{fk}}\).

definitions.name: Positive invariant-noise collider family
definitions.construction: For \(p=3\), factor \(\boldsymbol\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}\) under the common orders \(X\prec W\prec Y\) and \(W\prec X\prec Y\). For either order use environment \(1\) as baseline, set \(\mathcal I_1=\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal I_2=\{Y\}\), and change only the two baseline-parent coefficients into \(Y\). Both constructions induce the same difference DAG \(X\to Y\leftarrow W\), while the invariant \(X\)--\(W\) baseline edge is oriented according to the chosen common order and is absent from the difference DAG.

definitions.name: Bounded Gaussian tangent decision problem
definitions.construction: At a point with \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\), analyze the bounded experiment \(\{\mathcal N(h,V_0):(b,h)\in\Lambda_R\}\) with branch target \(\eta_b(h)\), Effros-measurable randomized closed-set rules \(\delta(\mathbb Y_h,U)\), uniform coverage class \(\mathfrak D_R\), and risk \(\mathfrak R_R\); characterize possible minimizers without fixing a candidate rule or proof method.

definitions.name: Full Bystrova--Devijver anchor class
definitions.construction:
Define \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{BD}}\) to be the class of baseline-indexed paired linear acyclic SCMs \(M\) for which \(\text{ass:linear-structural-equations}\), \(\text{ass:baseline-parent-containment}\), \(\text{ass:modular-interventions}\), and \(\text{ass:diff-faithfulness}\) hold, the coordinates \((\varepsilon_{e,v})_{v\in\mathbb V}\) are mutually independent for each \(e\in\mathbb E\), and the full exogenous-vector laws are invariant across environments:
\[
 \operatorname{Law}(\varepsilon_1)=\operatorname{Law}(\varepsilon_2).
\]
No Gaussian restriction is imposed in this definition.

definitions.name: Coefficient/covariance-bounded diff-faithful SCM subclass
definitions.construction:
Fix \(B\ge1\), set \(K_B=2B^2+4\) and \(\kappa_B=K_B^{-2}\), and define
\[
 \mathcal M_{p,B}^{\mathrm{df}}
 =\left\{M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}:
 \max_{e\in\mathbb E}\max_{u,v\in\mathbb V}|B_{e,uv}|\le B,
 \quad
 \kappa_B I_p\preceq\Sigma_{M,e}\preceq K_BI_p
 \text{ for every }e\in\mathbb E\right\}.
\]
No separation or beta-min condition is part of this subclass.

definitions.name: Bounded compatible-completion direct-effect fiber
definitions.construction:
For \(s\in\Omega_p\), define the coefficient/covariance-bounded compatible-completion fiber by
\[
 \Psi_B(s)
 =\overline{\{\tau(M):M\in\mathfrak F(s)\cap
 \mathcal M_{p,B}^{\mathrm{df}}\}}\subseteq\mathbb R^3.
\]
Thus the observable covariance coordinate is held fixed, and only completions belonging to the declared bounded subclass are retained.

definitions.name: Bounded projected-Wishart confidence union
definitions.construction:
Project the same exact paired Wishart covariance region through the bounded fiber:
\[
\widehat{\mathcal C}^{B}_{n,\gamma}
 =\overline{\bigcup_{s:\operatorname{vech}^{-1}(s)
 \in\mathcal R_{n,\gamma}}\Psi_B(s)}.
\]

statements.statement: For every \(M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\), the population covariance coordinate \(s(M)\) generates a complete ledger \(\mathcal L(s(M))\) for which BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC Theorem 1 retains the skeleton of the typed difference DAG \(D(M)\) and records only orientations present in \(D(M)\). Consequently \(D(M)\) is compatible with \(H(s(M))\), \(M\in\mathfrak F(s(M))\), and \(\tau(M)\in\Psi(s(M))\).
statements.justification: This lemma connects the discovery guarantee to coverage of the fixed causal target.
statements.gap: BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC Theorem 1 proves population recovery of the difference-DAG skeleton and sound orientations under its Definitions 2--4 and diff-faithfulness, but does not state the induced effect-fiber retention result.
statements.consumer: The finite-sample confidence theorem uses retention to cover the BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B direct-effect triple rather than a selected regression surrogate.

statements.statement: Under the two-sample Gaussian law, \(\nu_e\widehat\Sigma_e\sim\operatorname{Wishart}_p(\Sigma_{M,e},\nu_e)\) independently over \(e\in\mathbb E\). Hence \(\Pr_M\{\boldsymbol\Sigma_M\in\mathcal R_{n,\gamma}\}=1-\gamma\) for every \(M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) and every \(n_1,n_2>p\).
statements.justification: The exact pivotal event supplies honesty without beta-min or strong-faithfulness margins.
statements.gap: StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 gives an explicit asymptotic union-of-intervals confidence set for one scalar total effect under unknown single-environment equal-error-variance Gaussian DAG structure, establishing test inversion, structure unioning, and closed-form confidence construction as prior art. WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets uses residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests in identifiable additive-error structural equation models to obtain asymptotic causal-order confidence sets and model-uncertainty effect intervals. Neither provides the exact paired unrestricted-covariance Wishart pivot needed before two-environment LDiffPC fiber projection.
statements.consumer: Analysts can calibrate the causal union at a declared finite-sample level before any ledger decision is made.

statements.statement: For fixed \(p\), the graph of \(s\mapsto\Psi(s)\) over \(\Omega_p\) is a finite union of semialgebraic graphs \(\{(s,\theta_b(s)):s\in\mathcal S_b\}\), indexed by \(b\in\mathbb B_p\). Every \(\mathcal S_b\) has an explicit quantifier-free description obtained from the baseline-parent, modularity, invariant-noise, positivity, diff-faithfulness, exact-ledger, typed difference-DAG, and LDiffPC-compatibility constraints, and every coordinate of \(\theta_b\) is a rational predecessor-set regression with denominators nonzero on \(\mathcal S_b\).
statements.justification: A finite rational stratification makes discontinuous post-ledger inference mathematically tractable.
statements.gap: BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC gives a discovery algorithm, StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 explicitly unions intervals over unknown single-environment equal-error-variance DAG structures, and WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets builds asymptotic causal-order confidence sets from residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests in identifiable additive-error structural equation models. None gives the finite semialgebraic branch representation of a two-environment LDiffPC equality/sepset direct-effect fiber.
statements.consumer: The representation supplies the exact branch list used by the confidence union and its boundary limit law.

statements.statement: For every \(p\ge3\), \(n_1,n_2>p\), and \(0<\gamma<1/2\), the test-inverted union obeys \(\inf_{M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}}\Pr_M\{\tau(M)\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}\}\ge1-\gamma\). The infimum permits sequences on which nonzero regression-equality, conditional-independence, and completion-separation margins converge jointly to zero. The procedure assumes neither a known ledger nor a unique order or branch, conditions on no selected LDiffPC output, and imposes no beta-min or separation margin.
statements.justification: This is the boundary-honest coverage guarantee missing from plug-in post-LDiffPC inference.
statements.gap: StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 establishes asymptotic test inversion and structure unioning for one scalar total effect under unknown single-environment equal-error-variance Gaussian DAG structure; WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets gives asymptotic causal-order confidence sets and post-processed effect intervals in identifiable additive-error structural equation models; ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostSelection Theorem 2 gives asymptotic coverage after ordinary conditional-independence discovery; and GuoWuYiu2026Price gives exact selective coverage for a selected adjustment functional after Gaussian FCI when the variance is known. None gives exact unconditional coverage for a fixed paired direct-effect triple over a two-environment LDiffPC equality/sepset completion fiber.
statements.consumer: The ovarian-cancer BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B comparison can report one joint confidence union for the two direct effects and their change while retaining ledger uncertainty.

statements.statement: Let \((M_N)\) be a local model sequence with \(s(M_N)=s_0+h/\sqrt N+o(N^{-1/2})\) in a true branch \(b_0\). Under tangent-cone regularity, \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}\Rightarrow\mathcal K_h^{(0)}\) in the Fell topology. If \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\), then \(\sqrt N(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}-\tau_0)\Rightarrow\mathcal K_h^{(1)}\) in the Fell topology. The limit is derived from the paired Gaussian covariance central limit theorem, the exact Wishart acceptance bodies, and the rational branch representation; branch smoothness is a derived conclusion rather than an assumption.
statements.justification: The random-set law describes exactly which causal branches survive under simultaneous local ledger ambiguities, with branch regularity derived from the rational fiber representation.
statements.gap: Geyer1994Constrained derives cone limits for constrained estimators, StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood gives an asymptotic structure-unioned interval, WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets gives asymptotic causal-order confidence sets and post-processed effect intervals, and ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostSelection gives coverage and oracle equivalence under a strong signal lower bound. None derives the jointly local branch-cone random-set law at simultaneous LDiffPC equality, conditional-independence, and completion boundaries.
statements.consumer: The limit law yields boundary-aware critical-value and width calculations for LDiffPC compatible-completion effect reports.

statements.statement: If \(s_0\) lies in the relative interior of one branch cell and \(\mathbb B(s_0)=\{b_0\}\), then, for \(y=h+\mathbb Z_0\), \(\mathcal K_h^{(0)}=\{\theta_{b_0}(s_0)\}\) when \(T_{b_0}(s_0)\cap\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)\neq\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal K_h^{(0)}=\varnothing\) otherwise, while \(\mathcal K_h^{(1)}=\mathcal P_{\gamma}(y;b_0,s_0)=J\bigl(T_{b_0}(s_0)\cap\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)\bigr)\), where \(J=D\theta_{b_0}(s_0)=(J_1,J_2)\). If, in addition, \(s_0\) lies in the ambient interior of \(\mathcal S_{b_0}\), then \(T_{b_0}(s_0)=\mathbb R^d\) and \(\mathcal P_{\gamma}(y;b_0,s_0)=J\mathcal A_{\gamma}(y)=J_1\mathcal A_{1,\gamma}(y_1)\oplus J_2\mathcal A_{2,\gamma}(y_2)\); if \(\mathcal A_{e,\gamma}(y_e)=y_e+E_{e,\gamma}\), this equals \(Jy+J_1E_{1,\gamma}\oplus J_2E_{2,\gamma}\). The ambient-interior image is generally a Minkowski sum rather than a joint Wald ellipsoid. Because every branch target satisfies \(\tau_3=\tau_1-\tau_2\), \(\operatorname{rank}(J)\le2\); no rank assumption is required.
statements.justification: The reduction gives the exact regular-stratum geometry by retaining the branch tangent cone and isolates the product-score Minkowski formula as an ambient-interior corollary.
statements.gap: This is an internal special-case check rather than a novelty claim: the proposition records the cone-intersected score image and its ambient-interior product-score reduction, with differentiability now derived from the rational branch formula.
statements.consumer: Software can evaluate the regular-stratum limit by intersecting the score body with the branch cone and, only at ambient-interior points, mapping the two environment-specific score ellipsoids separately and taking their Minkowski sum.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(p\ge3\) and every \((a,b)\) in the chain--fork parameter space, the construction in \(\text{def:chain-fork-witness}\) gives two models \(M^{\mathrm{ch}},M^{\mathrm{fk}}\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) with the same law pair
\[
 \bigl(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)\oplus I_{p-3}),
 \mathcal N(0,\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)\oplus I_{p-3})\bigr).
\]
Here \(I_0\) denotes the empty covariance block.  The models have the same empty difference DAG, the same complete equality ledger, and the same empty population LDiffPC output, but \(\tau(M^{\mathrm{ch}})=(a,a,0)\) and \(\tau(M^{\mathrm{fk}})=(0,0,0)\).  For every ordered pair of distinct vertices and every eligible conditioning set, each model satisfies diff-faithfulness.  Therefore every procedure \((D_N)\) having coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) for both models satisfies
\[
 \Pr\{\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\ge\sqrt2|a|\}\ge1-2\gamma
\]
for every \(N\).
statements.justification: The dimension-uniform unbounded same-law family proves both fixed-separation noncontraction and infinite global worst-case expected diameter for every p at least three, distinguishing information-theoretically necessary width from conservatism of the confidence construction.
statements.gap: ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostSelection notes that its union may be wide and leaves minimal inflation open; it does not give an exact same-law lower bound, much less a dimension-uniform infinite global expected-diameter lower bound, for a paired direct-effect triple.
statements.consumer: Practitioners receive a formal abstention certificate when a wide BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B union reflects indistinguishable causal orders rather than numerical failure; the infinite conclusion is worst-case over each unrestricted p-dimensional class, not pointwise at that application.

statements.statement: For \(p=3\) and \(\boldsymbol\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}\), both covariance matrices have determinant \(4277/6250=0.68432\). Exactly the common orders \(X\prec W\prec Y\) and \(W\prec X\prec Y\) yield invariant innovation variances, and both give \(1,91/100,94/125\). Under the first order the coefficients into \(Y\) are \((B_{1,XY},B_{1,WY})=(2/5,1/5)\) and \((B_{2,XY},B_{2,WY})=(-1/10,3/5)\), and the second order gives the same four coefficients. With environment \(1\) as baseline and \(\mathcal I_2=\{Y\}\), each displayed completion belongs to \(\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{df}}\), induces \(D(M):X\to Y\leftarrow W\), and has a complete diff-faithful ledger compatible with the same collider-oriented \(H(s)\). Every member of the three-variable completion fiber has one of these two environment-specific ordered Cholesky factorizations, although its auxiliary baseline coefficients and intervention-target labels need not equal those of the displayed representatives. Consequently \(\Psi_3(\operatorname{vech}(\boldsymbol\Sigma^{\mathrm{col}}))=\{(2/5,-1/10,1/2)\}\). This statement makes no embedding or fiber claim for \(p>3\).
statements.justification: The audit shows that unresolved orientation need not force a wide effect union when all accessible environment-specific factorizations agree on the direct effect.
statements.gap: BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC proves sound collider orientation abstractly but does not give this exact invariant-noise, same-ledger, effect-fiber calculation.
statements.consumer: The example is a unit test for an implementation that must return a singleton effect target while preserving structural ambiguity.

statements.statement: Fix \(s_0\) with \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\) and a finite \(R>0\). In the experiment \(\mathbb Y_h=h+\mathbb Z_0\sim\mathcal N(h,V_0)\), indexed by \((b,h)\in\Lambda_R\) with target \(\eta_b(h)=D\theta_b(s_0)h\), is \(v_R=\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_R}\sup_{(b,h)\in\Lambda_R}\mathbb E_h[\operatorname{diam}(\delta(\mathbb Y_h,U))]\) attained by an Effros-measurable randomized closed-set rule, and can the attaining rules or the value \(v_R\) be characterized? If such a rule exists, does it admit a finite-sample pullback that remains uniformly \(1-\gamma\) honest over \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) and has strictly smaller expected diameter than \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}\) for at least one \((n,M)\), without weakening coverage elsewhere? The handle is the bounded branch-labelled decision problem in \(\text{def:local-minimax-handle}\).
statements.justification: Attainment and characterization of minimum expected diameter are the genuinely open content after honesty and the boundary experiment have been characterized.
statements.gap: StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 gives a closed-form asymptotic structure-unioned confidence set, WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets post-processes an asymptotic causal-order confidence set into model-uncertainty effect intervals, ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostSelection leaves minimal interval-width inflation unresolved, and GuoWuYiu2026Price derives a selective truncated-Gaussian construction for a selected adjustment functional. None addresses attainment or characterization of the bounded, unconditional, branch-labelled random-closed-set infimum, or an honest finite-sample pullback that is strictly shorter somewhere.
statements.consumer: A solution would turn the valid but conservative BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B projection union into an efficiency-certified reporting procedure.

sampling_model.design: Two independent observational samples from centered positive linear-Gaussian acyclic SCMs in \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\), with baseline-parent modular interventions and invariant innovation variances.
sampling_model.units: Within environment \(e\), \(Z_{e1},\ldots,Z_{en_e}\) are independent and identically distributed; the two environment samples are independent.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X\) is an endogenous observed exposure; there is no randomized assignment.
sampling_model.overlap: Positive innovation variances imply positive-definite covariance matrices; no propensity-score condition is used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The nuisance is the covariance pair together with its discontinuous exact equality and sepset ledger. The procedure inverts exact Wishart covariance pivots and recomputes every compatible ledger, LDiffPC output, and direct-effect fiber inside the covariance region.

estimand_functional: The observed-law partial-identification map is \(s\mapsto\Psi(s)\), and inference projects the exact paired covariance region through that map: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}=\overline{\bigcup_{s:\operatorname{vech}^{-1}(s)\in\mathcal R_{n,\gamma}}\Psi(s)}\). On the bounded subclass, the corresponding map is \(s\mapsto\Psi_B(s)\) and the projection is \(\widehat{\mathcal C}^{B}_{n,\gamma}\).
target_estimand: The primary causal target is the compatible-completion direct-effect fiber \(\Psi(s)=\overline{\{\tau(\widetilde M):\widetilde M\in\mathfrak F(s)\}}\). The fixed true causal triple is a retained member: \(\tau(M)\in\Psi(s(M))\) for every \(M\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\).

tldr: The proposal treats the complete LDiffPC equality and sepset ledger as a discontinuous nuisance rather than a selected truth. It projects an exact paired Wishart covariance region through every diff-faithful baseline-intervention completion whose typed coefficient-change DAG \(D(M)\) agrees with the partial difference graph, giving finite-sample coverage of the fixed environment-specific direct-effect triple as equality, conditional-independence, and competing-completion margins vanish. A finite semialgebraic branch representation yields a random-closed-set limit law under \(N^{-1/2}\)-local approaches to joint ledger boundaries. A same-law chain--fork family proves that noncontraction is sometimes information-theoretically necessary, while an exact \(p=3\) collider audit shows that unresolved orientation can leave \(\Psi_3\) singleton. The open question asks whether the precisely defined bounded Gaussian expected-diameter infimum is attained and whether an attaining rule has a strictly shorter honest finite-sample pullback.

project_justification.gap: BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC supplies population discovery of a typed difference DAG from cross-environment regression equalities but no effect inference. StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 establishes asymptotic test inversion, structure unioning, and an explicit confidence construction for one scalar total effect under unknown single-environment equal-error-variance Gaussian DAG structure; StriederDrton2023Confidence treats the same single-environment total-effect setting; WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets uses residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests in identifiable additive-error structural equation models to obtain asymptotic causal-order confidence sets and post-processed model-uncertainty effect intervals; ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostSelection gives asymptotic screening-union coverage after ordinary conditional-independence discovery; GraduZrnicWangJordan2025ValidInference targets an effect indexed by a randomized selected graph; and GuoWuYiu2026Price gives exact selective coverage for a selected adjustment functional after Gaussian FCI with known variance. None supplies the exact paired unrestricted-covariance Wishart pivot, the two-environment LDiffPC equality/sepset direct-effect fiber, exact unconditional coverage for a fixed direct-effect triple, the jointly local branch-cone boundary random-set law, or a same-law width lower bound for that fiber.
project_justification.niche: The paired Gaussian model has an exact finite-sample covariance pivot and a finite semialgebraic causal-fiber map. Together they permit unconditional inference for a fixed direct-effect triple without selecting a ledger, followed by a precise tangent-cone analysis of the resulting random set.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact uniform coverage, derives the zeroth- and first-order boundary random-set limits, gives the exact cone-aware score-image reduction on a regular singleton branch and its product-score form at ambient-interior points, and certifies an exact observational-equivalence lower bound. It leaves the genuinely nonroutine optimal-width acceptance-region problem explicit.

related_work: BystrovaDevijver2026LDiffPC Definitions 1--4 define the baseline-oriented difference DAG, diff-relevant paths, conditionally diff-relevant paths, and diff-separation, and Theorem 1 proves population LDiffPC recovery under diff-faithfulness; its endpoint is a partially directed difference graph rather than post-discovery inference for a causal coefficient. StriederDrton2023Confidence jointly tests unknown equal-variance DAG structure and a single-environment total effect, including a finite-sample split-likelihood construction, but does not involve paired regression-equality ledgers or direct-effect changes. StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood Theorem 2 and Sections 2.2--3.3 give an explicit asymptotic union-of-intervals confidence set for one scalar total effect under unknown single-environment equal-error-variance Gaussian DAG structure. That result establishes test inversion, structure unioning, and closed-form confidence construction as prior art for the first three theorems here; it does not supply an exact paired unrestricted-covariance Wishart pivot, a two-environment LDiffPC equality/sepset direct-effect fiber, exact unconditional coverage for a fixed direct-effect triple, or a jointly local branch-cone boundary random-set law. WangKolarDrton2023ConfidenceSets uses residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests in identifiable additive-error structural equation models to construct asymptotically valid causal-order confidence sets and post-processes them into effect intervals that incorporate model uncertainty. It does not give the exact paired unrestricted-covariance Wishart projection, the two-environment LDiffPC equality/sepset direct-effect fiber, the branch-cone random-set law, or the same-law noncontraction bound. ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostSelection unions graph-specific intervals over perturbed PC runs and covers a fixed effect asymptotically; its oracle-equivalence theorem requires a strong lower bound on nonzero associations, and its discussion leaves minimal interval inflation open. GraduZrnicWangJordan2025ValidInference uses randomized discovery and max-information to protect inference for a graph-indexed target, which differs from the fixed true direct effect here. GuoWuYiu2026Price derives exact finite-sample selective coverage, under known outcome variance and its stated Markov-blanket condition, for a selected adjustment functional after Gaussian FCI; the present target is instead a fixed paired direct-effect triple and coverage is unconditional over every LDiffPC-compatible completion. Geyer1994Constrained supplies the tangent-cone asymptotic template, but not a union of causal branches or a random closed-set effect limit. Assaad2025DifferenceGraphs identifies direct effects from a given difference graph and motivates the BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B consumer; it does not account for statistical uncertainty in a learned partial equality ledger. WangSquiresBelyaevaUhler2018DCI supplies the invariant multi-environment linear-Gaussian setting and the ovarian-cancer data lineage.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact covariance projection may be computationally expensive because every candidate covariance induces a fresh equality ledger and compatible-completion fiber. The proposal makes no polynomial-time claim. At boundary points with distinct elements of \(\Gamma(s_0)\), the confidence union generally has a non-singleton zeroth-order limit; Theorem 4 shows that this behavior can be unavoidable. Open-ended Question 1 asserts no convex-duality representation, least-favorable prior, attainment, strict improvement, or solution. Its possible finite-sample improvement is not a theorem.
honest_scope: The uniform coverage theorem is finite-sample and ranges over positive diff-faithful baseline-parent modular interventions with invariant Gaussian innovation variances; it assumes no known ledger, unique order, unique branch, beta-min condition, or uniform margin away from the excluded non-diff-faithful laws. The random-set limit is pointwise along \(N^{-1/2}\)-local sequences satisfying standard tangent-cone regularity and branch smoothness. The collider audit and its singleton statement concern only \(p=3\); no embedding or conclusion for \(p>3\) is claimed. The proposal does not assert the exhausted componentwise uniform-single-door necessity frontier, fixed-treewidth tractability, latent-variable robustness, optimal-width attainment, or a strictly improved pullback. On a unique relative-interior branch, Proposition 1 retains the branch tangent cone in the first-order score image; only at an ambient-interior point does it reduce to the linear image of the product of the two environment-specific score bodies, generally a Minkowski sum rather than a joint Wald ellipsoid. The BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B application is a reporting consumer, not evidence that its empirical ledger satisfies the maintained causal assumptions.
